questions.question_text: Why is it necessary to be clean? (what does cleanness enable / uncleanness cost)

findings.finding_value: WHY CLEANNESS IS NECESSARY: not for the person's own benefit but RELATIONALLY. The purpose-coding across the book returns BELONGING first (be holy as I am holy; that you should be mine - 20:26), then PROTECT-THE-HOLY (a holy God dwells in the midst; uncleanness would defile his sanctuary and kill - 15:31), then ACCESS (to approach / eat the holy - 22:4-7) and DANGER-AVERSION (lest they die). Cleanness exists because the Holy One dwells among them and they are HIS.

questions.question_text: Where does the concept of "unclean" come from? (source + root sense)

findings.finding_value: WHERE UNCLEAN COMES FROM: the source-coding clusters at the boundaries of LIFE and DEATH - the corpse (mortuary), the body's life-fluids and their loss (discharge, menstruation, semen, childbirth = genital-bodily), disease as a living-death (skin-disease/tzaraat, the largest bodily source), and the table (dietary) - together with MORAL/CULTIC rupture (sin, sexual sin, idolatry, sacrilege), which is the single largest source-domain (164 spans). The common thread: contact with death or loss of life-wholeness, and moral fault. Uncleanness is what is incompatible with the God of life.

questions.question_text: Why cover the unclean rather than scrub it clean? (reset x source_domain)

findings.finding_value: WHY COVER, NOT SCRUB (the key finding): the RESET is graded by GRAVITY, and the RESULT-WORD is domain-specific. Light contact uncleanness (carcass, corpse, menstrual-contact) is reset by SCRUBBING + WAITING alone (wash/launder/until-evening) - never covering. Graver states (skin-disease, abnormal discharge, childbirth) AND all MORAL fault require BLOOD/ATONEMENT (kaphar = literally 'to cover') + sacrifice. The mechanism (cover) can be shared, but the OUTCOME differs by state: bodily defilement ends in TAHER (you are CLEAN); moral fault ends in SALACH (you are FORGIVEN). You are made clean of the body, forgiven of sin - two categorically different resolutions. The Day of Atonement (16:30) is the single bridge verse where cleansing-language (taher) is applied to sin. So covering is reserved for what a wash cannot reach: the deep, the persistent, and the moral.

questions.question_text: Is the need to be clean IB-desire, external expectation, or prerequisite?

findings.finding_value: IS CLEANNESS IB-DESIRE, EXTERNAL, OR PREREQUISITE: it is NEVER driven by the inner being's own desire - the driver-coding returns ZERO volition. It is EXTERNAL COMMAND (141 spans) or DIVINE-INITIATIVE (19; 'I the LORD sanctify you' 20:8). The person is roughly half PASSIVE (atonement done FOR him) and half ACTIVE (he washes, confesses, afflicts himself). Cleanness is a required PREREQUISITE for belonging and access, imposed by the holy God's presence - the self does not want it for its own sake; it is owed to the God who dwells there.

questions.question_text: Does awareness of unclean come into play?

findings.finding_value: DOES AWARENESS COME IN (the key split): awareness is DECISIVE for MORAL fault but IRRELEVANT for BODILY uncleanness. Moral sin is not activated or remediable until KNOWN - the ch4-5 pattern runs hidden (alam) -> 'when he comes to know it' -> realizes his guilt -> confesses (yadah). Bodily uncleanness, by contrast, defiles AUTOMATICALLY (awareness 'not-in-view' on every genital/mortuary/dietary occurrence) whether or not one knows. So the inner being's KNOWLEDGE matters only where the fault is moral; the body's states run mechanically. Guilt engages the interior; defilement does not.

questions.question_text: Is clean status past-only, or also forward-standing?

findings.finding_value: PAST-ONLY OR FORWARD: cleanness is MOMENTARY and PAST-DIRECTED - a repeatedly-restored baseline (until-evening, or a fixed 7/33/66-day period), constantly re-incurred and re-remedied, never a secured forward state. Dietary and disease classifications are STANDING (inherent to the animal / the condition). Moral atonement is RECURRING (the annual Day). By sharp contrast HOLINESS (the holy axis) is STANDING-FORWARD - a vocation to be maintained ('you shall be holy'). So the two must not be confused: CLEAN = a momentary reset of the immediate past; HOLY = a maintained forward standing.

questions.question_text: What is the inner being in Leviticus - the seat and locus (nephesh vs heart)?

findings.finding_value: THE SELF IN LEVITICUS is the NEPHESH - the living person/self held in a STATE - NOT the deliberating HEART. nephesh runs to ~50 spans in every sense (person, self, life, the-dead, life-in-blood); the heart (levav) appears only THREE times in the whole book (19:17 'do not hate your brother in your heart'; 26:36 a 'faint heart' in exile; 26:41 the 'uncircumcised heart' humbled). Leviticus does not psychologise the interior; it locates the person as a STATUS-BEARING SELF. And the state is borne not only by persons (377) but by objects, houses, land, garments, and the sanctuary itself - the inner condition is ENVIRONMENTAL as much as internal: a person, a people, a place can all be clean/unclean/holy.

GATE-1 RECOVERY (the moral/volitional vocabulary the curated seed had omitted): a span-orphan audit (verse_span_index vs the registered terms) surfaced 13 inner-being terms that were never registered and so were invisible to the first pass. Chief among them is ahev - 'you shall LOVE your neighbour as yourself' (19:18; and 'love the sojourner' 19:34) - the second great commandment, which the study had represented only obliquely (via natar 'grudge'). Also recovered: deror LIBERTY (25:10, the Jubilee proclamation), chaphash/chuphshah FREEDOM (19:20), neder/nadar VOW (the will's self-binding commitment, 7:16; 22:18-23; 27:2,8), barak the priestly BLESS-verb (9:22-23), ashaq/yanah OPPRESS (6:2-4; 25:14-17, the exploitation the fear-of-God restrains), zimmah DEPRAVITY (18:17; 19:29), panah TURN (to idols 19:4,31; 20:6 - and God's favourable turning 26:9). The correction matters for the whole picture: Leviticus's inner being is not only positioned in states of clean/holy/sin but is also SUMMONED to LOVE, freed into LIBERTY, and binds itself by VOW - the relational and volitional life the curated index had dropped. (Note: chesed 'steadfast-love' does NOT occur in Leviticus in that sense; its one instance, 20:17, is the homonym 'disgrace'.) Method note: this recovery was needed because Gate 1 - the index-driven span-orphan scan - had not been run on the Torah; it is now run for Leviticus, and flagged as a debt for Genesis/Exodus.

questions.question_text: How does atonement work - the blood/life mechanism?

findings.finding_value: ATONEMENT WORKS BY LIFE: kaphar (cover) is not lexical cleansing - it is the substitution of a LIFE. 'The life (nephesh) of the flesh is in the blood; I have given it on the altar to make atonement for your souls (nephesh); it is the blood that atones by the life' (17:11,14). Atonement covers the person by a life given for a life. On the Day of Atonement three distinct mechanisms operate together: kaphar (cover by blood), taher (cleanse), and the scapegoat that BEARS AWAY the confessed iniquity (avon) into the wilderness (16:21-22). The atonement/ritual words are thus the MECHANISM of reset - not themselves the inner-being state; the inner-being terminology is the clean/sin state that the mechanism resets (confirming the researcher's opening hypothesis).

REDEMPTION (gaal/geullah/padah) - recovered after an extraction gap (gaal/geullah were never registered as terms; the kinsman-redeemer vocabulary, 18 tokens in the text, was invisible until re-coded from verse_span_index). It centres on the KINSMAN-REDEEMER (go'el): a near relative may BUY BACK what poverty forced away - land, a house, and above all a PERSON sold into slavery (25:49 - uncle, cousin, or clan-relative may redeem him, or he redeems himself if he prospers) - RESTORING the lost one to freedom and family. Redemption also applies to what is dedicated to the LORD (ch27: redeem by valuation + a fifth), EXCEPT the cherem (devoted/banned thing) and the tithe, which are IRREDEEMABLE (27:28,33). Set beside atonement, the two complete each other: ATONEMENT (kaphar 17:11) covers the guilty before God by a LIFE given; REDEMPTION (gaal) buys the lost back into belonging by a PRICE paid by a kinsman. The nephesh is both atoned-for (life-for-life) and redeemable (bought back) - the seed of the biblical go'el/Redeemer theme (Ruth; Job 19:25; Isaiah 'the LORD your Redeemer').

questions.question_text: Does Leviticus reveal a divine interior (God's disposition)?

findings.finding_value: LEVITICUS DOES REVEAL A DIVINE INTERIOR - and it is the axis the whole system turns on. God has a nephesh (soul) that ABHORS or does-not-abhor his people (26:11 'my soul shall not abhor you'; 26:30 'my soul will abhor you'); a FURY/wrath (chemah 26:28); a settled PLEASURE in the rightly-given offering (the 'soothing/pleasing aroma' nichoach, 16 occurrences, and its withdrawal 26:31 'I will not smell your pleasing aromas'); and a REMEMBERING of the covenant that is the ground of all restoration (26:42,45). The clean/holy/sin system exists because a holy God with a real, responsive disposition dwells IN THE MIDST - the inner being the book most fully portrays is God's.

questions.question_text: What is the inner being's own act / the way back (affliction, confession, humbling)?

findings.finding_value: THE INNER BEING'S OWN ACT AND THE WAY BACK: the people's ONE required interior act in the whole ritual system is SELF-AFFLICTION - 'you shall afflict your souls' (anah nephesh) on the Day of Atonement (16:29-31; 23:27-32), an active self-denial, cut off if withheld. And the way back from the covenant-curse is wholly INTERIOR: they must CONFESS their iniquity (yadah) and their uncircumcised HEART be HUMBLED (kana, 26:40-41) - whereupon God REMEMBERS the covenant. Where the ritual acts on the person from outside (washing, blood, atonement done FOR him), these two - self-affliction and confessing/humbled repentance - are the inner being's own active turning, and they are the hinge on which mercy swings.
